cases.note: children come back in input order, not sorted by id or by name
a chart of one row, and an empty chart
loading again replaces the chart: nothing of the old rows is left
ids that look like numbers keep input order; names may repeat, hold spaces or be empty
ids are case sensitive and unknown ids give an empty list and an empty name
a deeper chain with a bushy middle
children arrive before their parents, three levels in reverse
several roots and several orphans, in input order; an orphan's subtree is not an orphan
a parent id that is empty is a root; a parent id that is only a name is an orphan
cycles start at the member that comes first in the input and follow the parent links
two cycles are listed by the position of their first member; rows below a cycle are not cycles and not orphans
a self-parent row is a cycle of one and is neither a root nor an orphan
a chart with no problems reports none, and a reload clears an old report
cycles are ordered by where they start in the input, not by id
the chain starts with the person and ends at the top, whatever the order of the rows
a manager of the other person is the lowest common manager; so is a person for themself
people in different trees have no common manager, and neither does an unknown id
the chain of an orphan ends at the orphan; the chain of a row on or below a cycle is empty
cousins meet at their grandparent
names sort by byte value: capitals before lowercase, digits before letters, a space before everything; equal names are ordered by id
larger subtrees come first; equal sizes fall back to the name and then the id
roots and orphans are the tops of the outline, ordered by the same rule as siblings
rows on or below a cycle are left out of the outline and have no subtree
an empty chart has an empty outline in every order
names with brackets and spaces are printed as they are; the id follows in brackets
the order of the rows changes the input order but not the name or size order
a chain of 1500 managers: a solution that recurses once per level runs out of stack
a wide chart: many siblings with ties on the name, ordered by id as text
two charts of 100000 rows: a chain 100000 managers deep, and a random one with orphans and cycles
